elements.element: Customer is not prohibited or restricted from soliciting any employees or personnel of the other party.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly provides that “neither party shall solicit for employment,” thereby imposing a non-solicitation restriction on Customer.

elements.element: The non-solicitation obligation is mutual and applies equally to both parties.
elements.evidence: The restriction applies to “neither party,” making it mutual.

elements.element: The restriction applies only to personnel directly involved in the services.
elements.evidence: It covers only an employee “who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.”

elements.element: The restriction lasts no more than 12 months from the end of each covered person’s involvement in the services.
elements.evidence: Although the clause refers to twelve months after the end of a person’s involvement, it also applies independently “[d]uring the term of this Agreement.” If a person’s involvement ends more than twelve months before the Agreement terminates, the restriction continues for the remainder of the term and therefore exceeds twelve months from that person’s end of involvement.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The proviso states that the restriction “does not apply to general advertisements.”

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches by covered personnel are excluded from the non-solicitation restriction.
elements.evidence: The proviso states that the restriction does not apply to “unsolicited approaches by such persons.”

elements.element: The clause does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that it “does not prohibit hiring” and removes the original no-hire restriction.

result.reason: The redline does not achieve the preferred position because Customer remains subject to a non-solicit. It also fails the fallback because the separate “during the term” language can extend the restriction beyond 12 months after an individual’s involvement ends. The other fallback features—mutuality, directly involved personnel, both carve-outs, and no no-hire—are present. The change is not minimal to a complete acceptable position because neither level is fully attained, although it does not appear to disturb unrelated commercial terms.
